claims.text: FCC/B2 eutectic HEAs exhibit a transient ductile-brittle-ductile transition during intermediate thermal aging.
Evolution of local chemical order within B2 domains transiently maximizes lattice friction for dislocation glide.
Phase boundaries change from coherent or semi-coherent interfaces to incoherent or rough interfaces during aging.
Incoherent or rough phase boundaries initially block dislocation transmission, whereas subsequent coarsening restores mechanical compatibility.
The initial eutectic HEA has a fine lamellar FCC/B2 microstructure.
The FCC constituent is mechanically soft and the ordered B2 constituent is mechanically hard.
High ductility and work hardening in the initial state arise from dislocation storage at phase boundaries.
Aging at approximately 400–600 °C drives short-range ordering and phase-boundary restructuring while avoiding significant grain coarsening and long-range secondary-phase precipitation.
A peak in the B2 local-chemical-order parameter occurs before phase coarsening dominates.
Peak B2 local chemical order together with incoherent or rough phase boundaries creates a high barrier to dislocation transmission.
Ordering transitions in the B2 phase increase the Peierls barrier for dislocation motion.
Prior simulations found that lattice-parameter differences among constituent atoms hinder partial-dislocation motion, causing hardening and reduced ductility in CoNiCrFeMn HEA nanowires.
Hard B2 regions in a fine lamellar AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic structure pin dislocation motion through the soft FCC regions and contribute to work hardening.
The combined lattice-friction and phase-boundary barriers lock up dislocations and cause brittle fracture.
At higher aging temperatures, local chemical order saturates or decreases and phase boundaries coarsen or become more compatible, enabling dislocation bypass or transmission and restoring ductility.
Ductility reaches a minimum when local chemical order peaks and phase boundaries are most incoherent, then recovers at longer aging times or higher temperatures.
The brittle regime features little plastic deformation in B2 and cleavage-like fracture at phase boundaries rather than grain-boundary embrittlement.
For AlCoCrFeNi systems, the proposed embrittlement regime lies around 400–600 °C, while grain coarsening dominates above 700 °C.
In annealed AlCo0.5Cr0.5FeNi, sigma phase was observed at grain boundaries in Cr-rich regions.
The initial B2 phase is less ordered or more coherent with the FCC matrix than it is after intermediate aging.
